title.narrative: Strengthened national capacity for evidence-based policy responses to unemployment and informal employment in Eswatini

description.narrative: Eswatini continues to face significant labour market challenges marked by persistently high unemployment and low labour force participation. In 2023, the national unemployment rate stood at 35.4%, with labour force participation at 50.8%, reflecting structural constraints in job creation, including a persistent mismatch between workforce skills and labour market demands. Youth are disproportionately affected, with unemployment at about 58% compared to the national average, and young women experiencing higher unemployment and inactivity than young men, while a large share of workers, particularly youth, women, and persons with disabilities remain in the informal economy where decent work deficits are widespread. Working in collaboration with the UN, the ILO is assisting Government and the Social Partners to conduct an employment diagnostic analysis to understand the nature of the deficiency in productive employment, with a view to inform a targeted and inclusive programme that will address some of the pressing employment challenges in the country. Furthermore, building on prior ILO support for skills anticipation and mismatch measurement capacity, effort is now directed to assist Government to institutionalize skills anticipation and the measurement of skills mismatches. Target groups are the youth, especially those not in employment, education, or training, women, persons with disability, workers in the informal economy, and key national institutions with a mandate on employment
